description:
Found by the fz-kdt.120 cold review (defect 4) and paid for twice, by the
fz-kdt.120 prototype (open_vars(params, args): a second walk over the raw
arguments to decide openness) and by the fz-kdt.184 prototype (upper bounds
collected from args while lower bounds come from the witnesses). types/
arrow_match.rs match_witness returns the PATTERN instantiated by what the
argument pinned, so an unbound pattern variable reappears inside the witness
and compares against itself, and anything the argument said at a
contravariant position is gone: match_arrow([[a], b, (a,b)->b], b, {},
[[int], int, (binary,int)->int]) hands the third witness back as
(a,int)->int -- `binary`, the upper bound on a, is unrecoverable from it. Any
analysis that asks "was this ground?" or "what did the argument say here?" of
a witness answers wrongly. Direction: a witness is the OBSERVATION (the
argument, possibly narrowed by the pattern's ground parts), never a restated
pattern; instantiate_match then reads lower AND upper bounds and openness
from ONE walk over (params, args), and both second walks (120's open_vars,
184's args pass) collapse. Sequence: it can land before 184 (184 then loses
its two-input asymmetry) or after both; measure the corpus either way (0
movers expected -- the projection is redundant on the corpus today).
title: overlapping_witnesses returns pattern-derived witnesses, not observations: an unbound pattern variable is written back into the witness and contravariant content is erased, so two tickets each needed a second walk over the raw arguments
